titulo: The internet lies on the ocean floor

cenas.fala: About every two days, an internet cable on the ocean floor breaks. And you never notice.
cenas.legenda: About every 2 days an internet cable on the ocean floor breaks. And you never notice.
cenas.fonte: TeleGeography, ICPC fault data (avg. 199 faults/yr since 2010)

cenas.fala: Your messages, your videos, your bank transfers. They cross oceans mostly through cables, not satellites.
cenas.legenda: Your messages, your videos, your bank transfers cross oceans mostly through cables, not satellites.

cenas.fala: There are about six hundred cable systems in the world.
cenas.legenda: There are about 600 cable systems in the world.

cenas.fala: Laid end to end, they run more than one point five million kilometers.
cenas.legenda: Laid end to end, they run more than 1.5 million kilometers.

cenas.fala: That is enough to wrap around the Earth thirty seven times.
cenas.legenda: That is enough to wrap around the Earth 37 times.

cenas.fala: And they break. About two hundred times, every single year.
cenas.legenda: And they break. About 200 times every single year.

cenas.fala: Not sharks. Not spies. More than eight in ten breaks come from fishing gear and ship anchors.
cenas.legenda: Not sharks. Not spies. More than 8 in 10 breaks come from fishing gear and ship anchors.

cenas.fala: The internet you think lives in the cloud actually rests on the seabed.
cenas.legenda: The internet you think lives in the cloud actually rests on the seabed.

cenas.fala: One and a half million kilometers of glass, lying in the dark.
cenas.legenda: 1.5 million kilometers of glass, lying in the dark.

cenas.fala: Should countries guard these cables like their borders? Comment yes or no.
cenas.legenda: Should countries guard these cables like borders? Comment YES or NO.

final.pergunta: Should countries guard these cables like borders?

legenda_post: About every two days a cable on the ocean floor breaks and the internet keeps going. 600 systems, 1.5 million km of glass, and most breaks come from fishing gear and anchors. Should countries guard these cables like their borders?
